## Scientific Goals

- Overall goal is to understand the full AD patho-physiological spectrum (preclinical to dementia) of DS-AD
- Determine primacy of genetic contributions to DS-AD pathobiology and phenotype
- Determine if trajectories of DS-AD pathobiology fit existing conceptual frameworks for sporadic AD
- Based on discovered pathobiology, we will identify possible treatment targets
- Discover and establish multi-domain biomarkers that will be useful for next-generation clinical trials

```{r}
assessments <- list(
  "Cognitive Battery" = rep("X", 8),
  "Neurological Exam" = rep("X", 8),
  "Informant Interviews" = rep("X", 8),
  "Chart Reviews" = rep("X", 8),
  "Blood Draw" = rep("X", 8),
  "MRI" = rep("X", 8),
  "Amyloid PET" = rep(c("X", ""), 4),
  "Tau PET" = rep(c("X", ""), 4),
  "FDG PET" = rep(c("", "X"), 4),
  "CSF (optional)" = rep(c("X", ""), 4),
  "Consensus" = rep("X", 8)
)

assessment_html <- paste0(readLines("html/assessments.html"), collapse = "\n")

assessment_rows <- purrr::imap_chr(
  assessments,
  \(vals, nm) {
    paste0(
      "<tr>",
      "<td>",
      nm,
      "</td>",
      paste0("<td>", vals, "</td>", collapse = ""),
      "</tr>"
    )
  }
) |>
  paste(collapse = "\n")

cat(
  glue::glue(
    assessment_html,
    timepoints = paste0("<th>", timepoints, "</th>", collapse = "\n"),
    assessments = assessment_rows,
    .open = "{{",
    .close = "}}",
  ),
  sep = "\n"
)
```

## Exploring ABC-DS Clinical Data

For ABC-DS Investigators and Staff...

- BDM Core has prepared a file in which selected LONI tables are merged into a single data file
  - Available in SAS, SPSS and Excel
  - SAS and SPSS versions are self-documenting (variable and value labels for coded variables)
  - Derived variables include BMI, incident dementia and MCI indicators
- The merged file may be used to determine data availability, planning, and exploratory analysis


*Before conducting analyses for use in publications or preparations, a formal data request must be submitted*

## Study Data Files

```{r study files, ft.align = "left"}
all_files <- list.files(
  Sys.getenv("ABCDS_LONI_DATA_DIRECTORY"),
  pattern = ".csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
toRemove <- "Controls|biospecimen|Codebook|Dictionary|Followup|Safety_labs|Study_Partner|MRI_Scan|omics|Brickman"
participant_files <- all_files[!grepl(toRemove, all_files)]

done_vars <- c(
  "Sample_Collection_-_Blood_19Feb2026.csv" = "paxdone",
  "Tau_PET_Scan_Information_19Feb2026.csv" = "tau_done",
  "Amyloid_PET_Scan_Information_19Feb2026.csv" = "amy_done"
)


count_subjects <- function(x) {
  if (basename(x) %in% names(done_vars)) {
    done <- rlang::sym(unname(done_vars[basename(x)]))
    vars <- c("subject_label", as.character(done))
  } else {
    vars <- "subject_label"
  }
  # fmt: skip
  subjects <- readr::read_csv(x, col_select = dplyr::all_of(vars), show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (ncol(subjects) > 1) {
    subjects <- dplyr::pull(dplyr::filter(subjects, !!done == 1), subject_label)
    table(table(subjects))
  } else {
    table(table(subjects[, 1, drop = TRUE]))
  }
}

clean_file_names <- function(files) {
  basename_files <- basename(files)
  bf_no_csv <- gsub("_19Feb2026.csv$|.csv$", "", basename_files)
  bf_add_spaces <- strsplit(bf_no_csv, split = "_")
  purrr::map_chr(bf_add_spaces, ~ paste(.x[1:(length(.x))], collapse = " "))
}

main_df <-
  purrr::map(
    participant_files,
    ~ {
      counts <- as.data.frame(count_subjects(.x))
      tidyr::pivot_wider(
        counts,
        names_from = Var1,
        values_from = Freq,
        names_prefix = "Observation "
      )
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    file = clean_file_names(participant_files),
    dplyr::across(dplyr::contains("Observation"), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x)),
    .before = 1
  )

to_show <- c(
  "Centiloid Analysis of PET Data",
  "ApoE Genotyping Results",
  "Cued Recall",
  "Consensus",
  "CSF Results",
  "Down Syndrome Mental Status Exam",
  "Health History",
  "Physical and Neurological Exam",
  "Sample Collection - Blood",
  "Amyloid PET Scan Information",
  "Tau PET Scan Information"
)


study_file_table <-
  main_df |>
  tibble::tibble() |>
  dplyr::filter(file %in% to_show) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::starts_with("Observation"),
    names_to = "observation",
    values_to = "count"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(file, desc(observation)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cumulative = cumsum(count),
    observation = paste0(gsub("Observation ", "", observation), "+"),
    .by = file
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-count) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "observation", values_from = cumulative) |>
  dplyr::rename(File = file) |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  flextable::width(j = 1, width = 3) |>
  flextable::width(j = 2:6, width = 1.3) |>
  flextable::align(j = 2:6, part = "all", align = "center") |>
  flextable::bold(i = 1, part = "header") |>
  flextable::add_header_row(
    values = c("", "Number of Observations"),
    colwidths = c(1, 6)
  )

study_file_table
```

## Function Factories

A function factory is a function that makes functions.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
new_abcds_reader <- function(pattern, include_demographics = TRUE) {
  force(pattern)
  force(include_demographics)

  function(
    directory = NULL,
    controls = FALSE,
    add_demographics = include_demographics
  ) {
    # Code Here
  }
}

read_neuro_exam <- new_abcds_reader("Physical_and_Neurological")
read_consensus <- new_abcds_reader("Consensus")
```

## Data Processing with Function Factories

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
read_athropometrics <- abcds:::new_abcds_reader(
  pattern = "Physical_and_Neurological",
  .f = function(data) {
    data <- tidyr::fill(data, ht, htu, .direction = "down")
    data$ht <- ifelse(data$htu == 1, data$ht * 2.54, data$ht)
    data$wt <- ifelse(data$wtu == 1, data$wt / 2.205, data$wt)
    data$bmi <- data$wt / (data$ht / 100)^2
    data[, c("subject_label", "event_sequence", "ht", "wt", "bmi")]
  }
)
str(read_athropometrics(add_demographics = FALSE))
#> tibble [1,455 × 5] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
#>  $ subject_label : num [1:1455] 10001 10001 10001 10001 10002 ...
#>  $ event_sequence: num [1:1455] 1 2 3 4 1 1 2 3 1 2 ...
#>  $ ht            : num [1:1455] 155 155 155 155 142 ...
#>  $ wt            : num [1:1455] 60.4 59 57.4 63.6 51.7 ...
#>  $ bmi           : num [1:1455] 25.2 24.6 23.9 26.5 25.6 ...
```

|nonmemory	| dspi1 + dsap1 + dsla2 + dsvs1 + dske1                   |
|dsmse_to2	| dspi1 + dsme1 + dsap1 + dsla2 + dsvs1 + dske1           |
|dsto2	    | dspi1 + colshbx + dsme1 + dsap1 + dsla2 + dsvs1 + dske1 |

## Retrieving and Evaluating the Equations

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
Variables <- c("colmemscr", "nonmemory", "dsmse_to2", "dsto2")

Equations <- c(
  "colshbx + dsme1",
  "dspi1 + dsap1 + dsla2 + dsvs1 + dske1",
  "dspi1 + dsme1 + dsap1 + dsla2 + dsvs1 + dske1",
  "dspi1 + colshbx + dsme1 + dsap1 + dsla2 + dsvs1 + dske1"
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: 1-2|5-17|6|7|9-15
EquationVariables <- unlist(strsplit(Equations, "\\s* \\+ \\s*"))
AllVariables <- unique(c(Variables, EquationVariables))

purrr::map2(Variables, Equations, .f = function(.x, .y) {
  current_values <- data[[.x]]
  expected_values <- rlang::eval_tidy(rlang::parse_expr(.y), data = data)
  checks <- current_values == expected_values
  if (any(!checks, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    indx <- which(!checks & !is.na(checks))
    result <- data[indx, c("subject_label", "site_initials", "event_code")]
    result$Variable <- .x
    result$Equation <- .y
    result$atri <- data[indx, .x, drop = TRUE]
    result$expected <- expected_values[indx]
    return(result)
  }
})
```

## Longitudinal Modeling and Cohort Comparison

</ul>

```{r} 
#| results: asis
set_speaker("dana")
```

## Longitudinal Analyses

- Our data is not equally spaced because it is not collected at the same exact time.
- Longitudinal analysis are generally focused on change /rates per time unit.
- All longitudinal models should use the latency variable (time from baseline) from our database as the time variable.
- All models should be controlled for site differences.
- All models that are testing differences over time between groups, should test that by including an interaction effect **time X group** and should be tested in a nested fashion: 
  - Model with interaction vs. model without interaction (via F-test).
- In a longitudinal model (mixed effects model,) site can be added as a random effect since we are not interested in site differences, but we only want to control the variability that is due to sites.

```{r} 
#| results: asis
set_speaker("dana")
```

## Comparisons Between Our ABC-DS Cohort and Other Cohorts

- When comparing cohorts, we should fit a single model to all the data.
- To test differences between cohorts an indicator variable should be included in the model that is indexing the cohort (A, B, etc.).
- Work with your statisticians, have them check the models, analysis and inference. 

<div class="custom-image">
  <img src="https://bhelsel.github.io/presentationsR/inst/images/articles/tudorascu2019comparison.png" width="80%"/>
</div>

```{r} 
#| results: asis
set_speaker("dana")
```

## Data Harmonization

- Plays a crucial role in our analyses.
- Recently we investigated differences based on methods that have been accepted by the imaging community as standard methods for data harmonization across sites/centers such as: partial volume correction and smoothing and compared those with Combat. **We have found significant differences between these methods.**
- Combat harmonization has also shown significant variability in effect sizes between amyloid positive and amyloid negative individuals.

```{r} 
#| results: asis
set_speaker("dana")
```
